OSINTdefender Taiwan’s Ministry of National Defense (MND) says two Russian Tu-95 'Bear' strategic bombers entered its air defense identification zone (ADIZ) from the south this morning, flew through airspace east of Taiwan, and exited northeast of Keelung. The MND released an image of one of the bombers taken from a Taiwanese F-16. This is the second such incident this week. On Monday, the MND reported two Russian military aircraft flying off the island’s east coast but did not identify their type. Japan reportedly protested to Moscow after two aircraft believed to be Russian violated its airspace the same day. The flights come as Russian President Vladimir Putin is in Shenzhen, China, for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit hosted by Chinese President Xi Jinping. Overall, 2 sorties of Russian Tu-95 aircraft were detected this morning. The aircraft entered #Taiwan's ADIZ from the south, flew through airspace east of Taiwan, and exited the ADIZ northeast of Keelung. The #ROCArmedForces have monitored the situation and responded accordingly. https://twitter.com/MoNDefense/status/2123305270394994777/photo/1 - 國防部 Ministry of National Defense, ROC(Taiwan) 🇹🇼 tweet
